title: Symmetric monoidal localization of a tensor-stable system
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging the ambient universe if necessary. Let $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ be a symmetric monoidal infinity category, encoded by a cocartesian fibration over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ whose fiber over the pointed set $\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ is identified by the inert projections with $\mathcal C^n$; inert means each non-basepoint of the target has exactly one preimage. Let $W$ be a collection of arrows of $\mathcal C$ containing all equivalences, closed under composition and homotopy, such that $X\otimes w$ and $w\otimes X$ lie in $W$ whenever $w\in W$ and $X\in\mathcal C$. There exist a symmetric monoidal infinity category $\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ and a strong symmetric monoidal functor $q^{\otimes}:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ with the following properties. Its underlying $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is the homotopy coherent localization at $W$: restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ carrying $W$ to equivalences, for every infinity category $\mathcal E$. For every symmetric monoidal $\mathcal E^{\otimes}$, restriction similarly identifies the infinity category of strong symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ to $\mathcal E^{\otimes}$ with the full subcategory of those from $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ carrying $W$ to equivalences. In particular
$$q(X)\otimes q(Y)\simeq q(X\otimes Y),\qquad \mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\simeq q(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}),$$
with coherent associativity, unit and symmetry constraints. This applies in particular to the symmetric monoidal nerve of an ordinary symmetric monoidal category.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7.4 and Remark 4.1.7.5 (printed pp. 485-486); Construction 4.1.7.1 fixes the system of arrows. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] to the stated system $W$. Denote its finite-product-preserving left adjoint by $L$, its fully faithful right adjoint by $G$, and its unit by $\eta$. Put $\mathcal D=L(\mathcal C,W)$ and let $q$ be the underlying component of $\eta_{\mathcal C,W}$. The cited full functor-category restriction equivalence gives the required underlying localization, including transformations and higher homotopies.

By [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification], classify $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ by a Segal diagram $F$. Mark $F(\langle n\rangle)\simeq\mathcal C^n$ with $W^n$. This gives a diagram $F_W:N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)\to\mathsf{WCat}_\infty$ as defined in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal]. Indeed, over $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$, the $j$th output is the tensor of the inputs with $\alpha(i)=j$. The tensor of finitely many arrows $w_i\in W$ is a composite of arrows changing one tensor factor at a time; each belongs to $W$ by tensor stability, so the composite belongs to $W$. A block with no input gives the identity of the unit, and an input sent to $*$ is discarded. Thus every $F(\alpha)$ preserves the coordinatewise systems. All functorial coherence equivalences also preserve them, since $W$ contains equivalences and is closed under homotopy and composition. The mapping spaces defining $\mathsf{WCat}_\infty$ are precisely unions of the corresponding components, so the entire coherent diagram lifts, with its given coherences.

source.place: Construction 4.1.7.1; the paragraph between Propositions 4.1.7.2 and 4.1.7.4; Definition 2.4.2.1 and Example 2.4.2.4.

proof.text: Form the actual diagram $LF_W$ by composition. Finite-product preservation in [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] identifies its inert comparison at every $n$ with $L((\mathcal C,W)^n)\simeq L(\mathcal C,W)^n$, also for $n=0$. Hence it is a Segal diagram. Unstraighten it by [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] to obtain $\mathcal D^{\otimes}$. Forgetting markings in the natural transformation $\eta F_W:F_W\to GLF_W$ gives a transformation of Segal diagrams, hence a strong symmetric monoidal functor $q^{\otimes}$; at $\langle1\rangle$ it is the $q$ of step 1. In particular the construction provides all the higher coherences, rather than only a binary tensor on a homotopy category.

source.place: The paragraph preceding Proposition 4.1.7.4 and Example 2.4.2.4; the product preservation is Proposition 4.1.7.2.

proof.text:
First prove the universal property on spaces of strong functors. For a symmetric monoidal target with Segal diagram $H$, the adjunction of [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf{Fin}_*),\mathsf{Cat}_\infty)}(LF_W,H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf{Fin}_*),\mathsf{WCat}_\infty)}(F_W,GH).$$
Explicitly, the forward map takes $t$ to $Gt\circ\eta F_W$ and the inverse takes $s$ to $\epsilon H\circ Ls$, with $\epsilon$ the counit. Their composites are homotopic to the identities by the adjunction triangle identities, componentwise and coherently by naturality. Segal diagrams form full subcategories of the diagram categories. A transformation on the right is exactly a transformation of the underlying Segal diagrams whose component at $\langle1\rangle$ sends $W$ to equivalences: its component at $\langle n\rangle$ is the product of that component, as follows by naturality for the inert projections. The classification of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] therefore identifies the displayed equivalence with restriction along $q^{\otimes}$ on spaces of strong symmetric monoidal functors inverting $W$.

source.place: The adjunction on commutative monoid diagrams in the paragraph preceding Proposition 4.1.7.4; Example 2.4.2.4 and Remark 2.4.2.6. The componentwise mate maps are written explicitly here.

proof.text:
To include noninvertible monoidal transformations, take any small infinity category $K$ and apply step 4 to the pointwise symmetric monoidal target $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ supplied by [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]. Its currying equivalence identifies the resulting spaces with
$$\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E))^{\simeq}\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\operatorname{Fun}^{\otimes}_W(\mathcal C,\mathcal E))^{\simeq}.$$
Here the subscript denotes the full subcategory on $W$-inverting functors: a morphism in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ is an equivalence precisely when all its components are equivalences, so its $W$ condition is exactly that every vertex of the $K$-diagram lies in this full subcategory. The displayed equivalences are the maps induced by the same restriction functor, naturally in $K$. They are equivalences on mapping spaces from every $K$ in $\mathsf{Cat}_\infty$. Explicitly, write $R:A\to B$ for restriction. At $K=B$, lift $1_B$ to $S:B\to A$, obtaining $RS\simeq1_B$. At $K=A$, the images of $SR$ and $1_A$ are equivalent, so full faithfulness of the mapping-space equivalence gives $SR\simeq1_A$. Thus $R$ is an equivalence. This proves the asserted full infinity-category universal property, with all transformations and higher homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.7.4(1); Remark 2.1.3.4 and Definition 2.1.3.7, with the parameter argument written out.

proof.text: The natural transformation of Segal diagrams constructed in step 3 commutes with the active maps $\langle2\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ and $\langle0\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$. Under the classification of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification], these squares give $q(X)\otimes q(Y)\simeq q(X\otimes Y)$ and $\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\simeq q(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$. Its naturality for every composite and every simplex of $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ gives the associativity, unit, symmetry and higher coherence constraints.

source.place: Definition 2.4.2.1, Remark 2.4.2.3 and Definition 2.1.3.7; the two squares of the constructed natural transformation.

proof.text: For an ordinary symmetric monoidal category $A$, [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] supplies the symmetric monoidal infinity category $N(A^{\otimes})$ with underlying $N(A)$. Regard a system of arrows of $A$ satisfying the stated tensor stability as a system in this nerve. Composition, equivalences and the tensor operations are the original ones, so all hypotheses checked in steps 1-3 apply. Steps 4-6 give the same localization and both universal properties for this nerve.
